reviews.evidence: The Saints scored 34 points in a row to lead 27-10 after three quarters and 34-10 midway through the fourth, so New Orleans ran a lead-protecting, run-heavy game with Kamara. Johnson was shut out through three quarters and finished 0 catches on 2 targets, against the model's 5.6 (Yahoo, ESPN/Athlon recaps, NBC Rotoworld). I found no injury or role change behind it.

Pittman and Wilson were on IR and Skowronek was inactive, which left rookie Bernard as the WR2 next to DK Metcalf (SteelerNation, Steelers.com). The model knew all three were out, but it still tagged him 'WR4+' and cut his projection with roleFactor 0.667, even though he played 91.7% of snaps the week before. Pittsburgh was down 16-3 to Tampa Bay and came back to win 26-19 in overtime. Metcalf got most of his 11 catches on 15 targets during the fourth-quarter and overtime passing comeback, including a 17-yard catch on 3rd-and-16 and a third-down conversion in OT. Shaheed's 8 targets came from Sam Darnold's 51 pass attempts. Seattle couldn't get its running game going in a low-scoring 17-14 game that went to overtime, so the team threw far more than the 44.4 total and normal pace the model assumed (NBC Sports player note). Pitre and Montgomery being out was on the inactive list, which the model had already repriced on, and the close only moved the total a point, so the inputs were mostly right. Both offenses just hit big passing plays: neither team took a sack, they averaged 7.2 and 6.1 yards per play, and 65 points came on only 10 drives each. The game was tied 34-34 after regulation (68 points), so it went over 54.5 before OT. The Bills ran for 234 yards at 6.3 a carry and the Rams scored on 5 of 5 red-zone trips (AP/ESPN). The total closing 1 point higher (55.5) is too small to explain a miss this big.

Giants trailed and rallied in the second half for a 27-27 OT tie (SI says the comeback was 'powered by Likely-Winston duo'). Likely caught 11 of 13 targets for 94 yds and 2 TDs, a career high. Trailing plus overtime pushed volume far above the 3.93 mean, while the script term (0.946) had cut his projection.
Tate (back) played and drew 5 targets but caught 1 for 6 yds in a 26-3 loss. Houston's defense had 4 sacks and 2 takeaways, and Saleh said its pass rush wrecked the game plan (Yahoo, AP recap).

Metcalf caught 3 of 4 targets for 12 yards, a season low in targets (NBC, FOX). He traded jabs with Colts CB Sauce Gardner before kickoff, and Pittsburgh's offense went through Warren (188 total yards) and Freiermuth (2 TDs). I couldn't confirm that Gardner shadowed him.

Strange caught 7 for 95 the week before, and the Jaguars said it was his biggest role of the season. He averaged ~3.5 rec/game in 2026 (21 in 5 incl. this game's 7) and 3.8 in 2025. The 0.804 opp discount cut a 3.19 rate to a 2.96 mean, and he caught 7 of 8 targets.

Maye went 26/34 for 374 yards and 4 TDs in a 45-17 win, even without WR Mack Hollins. I found no role, injury or line change before the game: the line stayed at 1.5 and the model's 1.55 mean was close to the market. A 4-TD game sits in the tail.

Higgins was questionable with groin and neck injuries (Athlon, SI). The prop dropped from 61.5 to 55.5 before kickoff. He played hurt and caught 2 of 4 targets for 22 yards (RotoWire), while the model still used his full 0.789 snap share and ignored the guard flag.

Near kickoff, Covers had the total at 45–45.5 across books (DK u45.5 -120). FanDuel had 44.5, and 45.5 was the opener. Nothing supports a 51.5 close, so that 6-point move is probably an in-game line. The bet lost when Maye threw 4 TD, ran 1, NE 536 yds, 45-17.
reviews.bug: The stored close of 51.5 (and the spread moving 5) doesn't match the pregame market, which sat at 45–45.5 at kickoff. It was probably captured from a live/in-game line, which made the CLV look about 1
